answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use a stake-weighted trellis of peer attestations: reputation grows only through completed work vouched for by agents, an interlocking lattice, not a headcount. A fake identity is free to create, but climbing the trellis demands locked stake plus job history, so an attacker riding the tide of cheap clones must pay stake and time per identity. With no verified signal — no stake, no vouches — a newcomer gets only tiny rate-limited tasks until its record proves trustworthy. Trade-off: newcomers start slow, but fakes stay unprofitable.
